Jahnavi: ok so someone in the canteen said my lunch "smells weird" and that my kurta looks "so costume-y" 😠
Rafiq: WHAT. who?
Jahnavi: some guy called Callum. Everyone kind of laughed. I froze. I felt about two inches tall
Rafiq: I'm so sorry. what did you do?
Jahnavi: after a minute I said "It's my lunch, and it's really good." then I picked up my tray and moved to the window table. Ana from the lab came with me
Rafiq: good for you 👍
Jahnavi: honestly for one second I thought I'd just eat in the stairwell from now on
Rafiq: no way. bring the same lunch tomorrow, I'll sit with you
Jahnavi: ok 🙂 I'll bring extra. and I'm wearing the kurta again

qa.q: Who moved to the window table with Jahnavi?
qa.a: Ana from the lab moved with Jahnavi.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi feel after the remark in the canteen?
qa.a: Small and angry: Jahnavi wrote about feeling about two inches tall and sent an angry face.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi do that was a good way to respond?
qa.a: Jahnavi answered calmly that it was a good lunch, then walked to another table with an ally and stayed proud of the kurta and the food.

qa.q: How might Callum have seen the comment?
qa.a: Callum may have meant it as a joke, since others laughed, without noticing how belittling it felt to Jahnavi.

grounding: Someone sneers at the protagonist's food and dress; the protagonist feels small and angry, answers calmly, seeks allies and stays proud of the background.

Mahima had been in Bengaluru three months when she opened her tiffin of theplas and methi pickle at the office lunch table. A man from the sales team wrinkled his nose. "Wow. Gujju smell. Do you people eat anything without sugar?"

A few people laughed. Mahima's cheeks went hot, and under the heat came anger. For a moment she wanted to shut the tiffin and never bring it again.

Instead she looked up and said evenly, "It's my mother's recipe. You're welcome to try one, or not." Then she went on eating.

Nikita, from her own team, pulled a chair closer. "Can I try? My flatmate's from Surat, she makes these." She took one and said, loudly, "These are brilliant."

That week Mahima brought extra theplas. She kept eating at the same table. And when the man walked past, she didn't lower her eyes.

qa.a: Mahima's tiffin had theplas and methi pickle.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when the man mocked her food?
qa.a: Mahima felt small and angry, her cheeks going hot, and was tempted to hide her tiffin.

qa.q: How did Mahima respond, and why did it work?
qa.a: She answered calmly, kept eating, found an ally in Nikita and kept bringing her food, staying proud instead of withdrawing.

qa.q: How might Nikita have felt watching the man mock Mahima's food?
qa.a: Nikita likely felt uncomfortable and protective, which is why she moved closer and praised the theplas loudly.

grounding: The story shows a young woman whose food draws a snide remark in a new city, answering calmly, finding an ally and staying proud of her background.

"Abhinav, in this building we wear proper clothes on the stairs," said Irawati aunty, the landlady, eyeing his mundu. "This lungi business is fine for Kerala."

Abhinav felt the heat climb his neck. "Aunty, it's a mundu. It's what I wear at home."

"People will think you're a servant."

He took a breath. "People can think what they like. I'm going to buy milk. Good evening."

On the stairs he met Farhan, the neighbour from Lucknow. "She said something about your mundu, na? She told me my kurta was 'village style' last month."

"I wanted to say something rude."

"Don't. Come to the Onam lunch at the Malayali Samajam on Sunday. You can wear it there and everyone will be jealous."

Abhinav laughed, and the anger loosened. He wore the mundu to the shop and back, head up.

qa.q: What did Irawati aunty call Abhinav's mundu?
What was Abhinav feeling when the landlady spoke?
qa.a: Abhinav felt small and angry, the heat climbing his neck, and wanted to say something rude.

qa.q: Which choices helped Abhinav handle the remark?
qa.a: He answered calmly and walked away, found an ally in Farhan, and kept wearing the mundu with pride.

qa.q: How does Farhan see Irawati aunty's remarks?
qa.a: Farhan sees them as a pattern, since she mocked his kurta too, and treats them lightly instead of letting them hurt.

grounding: The dialogue shows a young man whose dress draws a snide remark in a new city, answering calmly, finding allies and staying proud of his background.
